About Us

SharkNinja is a global product design and technology company, with a diversified portfolio of 5-star rated lifestyle solutions that positively impact people’s lives in homes around the world. Powered by two trusted, global brands, Shark and Ninja, the company has a proven track record of bringing disruptive innovation to market and developing one consumer product after another has allowed SharkNinja to enter multiple product categories, driving significant growth and market share gains. Headquartered in Needham, Massachusetts with more than 4,100 associates, the company’s products are sold at key retailers, online and offline, and through distributors around the world.

AI at SharkNinja

At SharkNinja, we’re building an AI-native culture. We’re not waiting for the future; we’re creating it. Our people are expected to experiment boldly, adopt new tools, and continuously raise what’s possible to create meaningful impact for our consumers. If you believe the best way to do your job hasn’t been invented yet, you’ll fit right in.

About the Role

Based remotely and reporting to the Sr. Vice President, Global Logistics, the Senior Manager, Continuous Improvement will play a critical leadership role in driving cost savings, service improvement, and operational excellence across SharkNinja's Operations organization. This individual will own the visibility, governance, and execution of initiatives that reduce cost, improve service, and unlock scalable efficiency across the business.

This role partners cross-functionally with Operations, Supply Chain, Logistics, Finance, Sales, Planning, and other key stakeholders to identify, prioritize, and deliver high-impact opportunities across the Operations expense base. The Senior Manager will own the Operations Efficiency project portfolio, ensuring initiatives are clearly defined, delivered on time, financially validated, and incorporated into forecast updates in partnership with Finance.

This is a highly visible, hands-on role for a strategic operator who can move seamlessly from executive-level portfolio management to deep analytical problem solving and cross-functional execution.

Other requirements:

  • Travel required (domestic & international) – up to 20%
  • Flexible work schedule to accommodate virtual meetings with other regions

What You'll Do

Own the Operations Efficiency Agenda

  • Lead the Operations Efficiency program across SharkNinja, serving as the central owner for cost savings, service improvement, and continuous improvement initiatives across the Operations expense base
  • Develop and manage the Operations Efficiency project portfolio, including opportunity identification, business case development, initiative prioritization, execution tracking, risk management, and benefits realization
  • Establish clear governance, routines, and reporting mechanisms to ensure initiatives remain on track, roadblocks are escalated quickly, and leaders have visibility to progress, savings, and risks
  • Act as a thought partner to Operations leadership by identifying where cost, service, process, or organizational improvements can unlock meaningful business value

Drive Cost Savings and Service Improvement

  • Identify opportunities to reduce Operations Expense while maintaining or improving service levels, customer experience, and operational reliability
  • Partner with Global Logistics to deeply understand distribution, transportation, delivery, warehousing, carrier, and network cost drivers
  • Lead cross-functional workstreams focused on improving cost-to-serve, delivery efficiency, network utilization, freight optimization, accessorial management, productivity, and service performance
  • Translate data and operational insights into actionable recommendations, business cases, and execution plans
  • Challenge existing ways of working and bring a continuous improvement mindset to how SharkNinja scales operations with speed, agility, and discipline

Partner Cross-Functionally to Deliver Results

  • Collaborate closely with Operations, Supply Chain, Finance, Sales, Planning, Consumer Experience, and other business partners to identify and execute opportunities
  • Build strong working relationships with Finance to ensure savings methodologies are aligned, benefits are validated, and impacts are reflected in forecast updates, budgets, and financial reporting
  • Create transparency across initiative owners, milestones, financial impacts, dependencies, and risks
  • Influence without authority across a fast-moving, matrixed organization, ensuring teams are aligned around common goals and accountable for delivery

Lead Continuous Improvement

  • Bring structured problem-solving, Lean, Six Sigma, or similar continuous improvement methods to complex operational challenges
  • Identify root causes of cost increases, service misses, process inefficiencies, and operational friction
  • Develop scalable processes, playbooks, and tools that improve how SharkNinja identifies, manages, and delivers efficiency opportunities
  • Create a culture of ownership, accountability, and speed in delivering operational improvements

What You'll Bring

The ideal candidate is a high-energy, analytical, commercially minded operator who thrives in a fast-paced environment — equally comfortable building an executive-ready savings roadmap, digging into logistics cost drivers, challenging assumptions, aligning Finance on benefit validation, and pushing cross-functional teams to deliver. This person brings a "CEO mindset" to Operations Expense: seeing the full picture, owning outcomes, making tradeoffs, driving accountability, and relentlessly pursuing better ways to deliver cost, service, and operational performance.

  • 7+ years of experience in Operations, Supply Chain, Logistics, Continuous Improvement, or a related field
  • Experience in consumer products, retail, eCommerce, durable goods, or high-growth global operations
  • Demonstrated experience leading cost reduction, operational efficiency, productivity, or transformation initiatives
  • Strong understanding of logistics, distribution, transportation, warehousing, delivery operations, and cost-to-serve drivers
  • Experience managing a portfolio of cross-functional initiatives with multiple owners, timelines, dependencies, and financial impacts
  • Proven ability to partner with Finance on savings validation, forecasting, budgeting, or financial performance tracking
  • Strong analytical skills with the ability to turn complex data into clear insights, recommendations, and action plans
  • Experience influencing cross-functional stakeholders and senior leaders in a fast-paced, matrixed environment
  • Background in Lean, Six Sigma, Kaizen, process improvement, or operational excellence
  • Proficient in Microsoft Project, Excel, PowerPoint, and Visio; experience with ERP/WMS/eCommerce platforms (e.g., SAP, Oracle, Shopify, Salesforce Commerce Cloud) a plus

Education: An undergraduate degree from a respected college/university, ideally in a discipline relevant to supply chain (e.g., Supply Chain Management or Engineering). A Master's degree in Business Administration or a technical discipline is not required but will further differentiate the ideal candidate.

Our Culture

At SharkNinja, we don’t just raise the bar—we push past it every single day. Our Outrageously Extraordinary mindset drives us to tackle the impossible, push boundaries, and deliver results that others only dream of. If you thrive on breaking out of your swim lane, you’ll be right at home.

What We Offer

We offer competitive health insurance, retirement plans, paid time off, employee stock purchase options, wellness programs, SharkNinja product discounts, and more. We empower your personal and professional growth with high impact Learning Programs featuring bold voices redefining what’s possible. When you join, you’re not just part of a company—you’re part of an outrageously extraordinary community. Together, we won’t just launch products—we’ll disrupt entire markets.

At SharkNinja, Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion are vital to our global success. Valuing each unique voice and blending all of our diverse skills strengthens SharkNinja’s innovation every day. We support ALL associates in bringing their authentic selves to work, making an impact, and having the opportunity for career acceleration. With help from our leadership, associates, and our community, we aim to have equity be a key component of the SharkNinja DNA.

jobs.excerpt: Our Mission at AMPECO is to enable the EV charging providers of tomorrow through innovative technology, and the vision we share is to build the platform of choice for large-scale EV charging providers globally.
jobs.description:
Our Mission at AMPECO is to enable the EV charging providers of tomorrow through innovative technology, and the vision we share is to build the platform of choice for large-scale EV charging providers globally.
At AMPECO, we empower businesses with innovative software solutions in e-mobility and energy. Our SaaS product, used by companies to manage their EV charging infrastructure, processes, and efficient energy use, is already making a difference across the UK, continental Europe, South and North America, Australia, and Asia.

Why will you enjoy this new opportunity?

    You love building software that genuinely matters — software that changes how an entire industry operates. You’re energized by hard problems, by clean architecture, and by the fact that the technologies you work with keep evolving, because that evolution is exactly what makes the work interesting. You’re excited rather than threatened by AI changing how software gets built, and you want to be on the leading edge of that shift — not watching it from the sidelines. You want to build software that real businesses depend on, not software that sits on a shelf.

    This role sits at the core of AMPECO, where our mission is to enable the EV charging providers of tomorrow through innovative technology. Our platform manages 300,000+ charge ports across 70 markets — critical infrastructure with 24/7 SLAs, used by charging businesses across the UK, continental Europe, the Americas, Australia, and Asia.

    We rebuilt our entire engineering process around our CoOperator Dev Agent (CODA): today it delivers 7× the features with the same team, with ~80% fewer bugs per feature. Engineers direct the work and own the quality bar by holding the final approval.

What type of work will you be doing?

    As a Software Engineer at AMPECO, you will:

    • Own the architecture and system design — set the technical direction our AI agents build within, and judge whether what they produce fits it. The platform is a global SaaS: a PHP/Laravel core, Node.js + TypeScript and Go microservices, and a React Native + TypeScript mobile app.
    • Groom stories side by side with product owners — this is the highest-leverage human step in our process. You’ll sharpen requirements into specs crisp enough to hand to the factory, and increasingly define and request features yourself, not just receive them.
    • Direct AI agents rather than type code: align on the what and the why up front, then validate the result — reviewing not just the final code but every artifact along the way: the implementation plan, the acceptance-test plan, the test evidence, and the agent’s proof of work.
    • Hold the final approval that closes every story — the human gate that keeps “frictionless” from becoming “uncontrolled” — and become a trusted voice in raising the quality bar for everyone.
    • Make every correction permanent: feedback you give in review gets codified into the system — skills, rules, and checklists — so the same mistake never has to be corrected twice. Our best engineers are the ones whose expertise the whole factory now runs on.
    • Contribute to CODA itself — refining agent instructions, strengthening automated quality guardrails, extending workflows with project-specific steps, and helping push the system further toward autonomous, zero-touch delivery.

What does a typical day look like?

    You wake up to a review stack: the stories you queued yesterday were implemented, tested, and pushed through CI overnight. Your morning is judgment work — reviewing plans and diffs, approving what’s proven, sending back what isn’t (your comments don’t just fix this story; they get mined to improve the factory). Midday you groom the next stories with your product owner — the one handoff we deliberately kept. You end the day by queueing the next batch so the factory runs while you sleep. Bugs flow through the factory just like stories — investigation, root cause, and fix are automated, and the review is yours. You choose when to review them, so bugs never break your flow.

What are we looking for?

    • Strong software engineering fundamentals — system design, API and data modeling, and the code-reading depth to review work you could have built yourself. You can’t direct what you couldn’t do.
    • Writing as a first-class skill: your specs and review feedback are your work product now.
    • Taste and judgment for quality — you notice what’s missing, not just what’s wrong.
    • Curiosity about the tooling itself: the engineers who thrive here treat the factory as a product they co-own, not a service they consume.
    • Experience with our stack is a plus — PHP/Laravel above all, and any of Node.js/TypeScript, Go, or React Native — but we care more about engineering depth than framework history.

Structure and culture of the team and leadership of the role

    You’ll join exceptional engineers whose best knowledge isn’t just in their heads — it’s encoded in the skills and rules the factory runs on. You learn from both; in time, your expertise joins the library. We run a flat structure with minimal hierarchy: decisions are made close to the work, ideas are judged on their merit rather than the title behind them, and every team member — whatever their level or discipline — is expected to take a leading role in how the team performs. You’ll have direct access to the people shaping the platform’s direction. We focus on iterative improvement, both of the software we build and the practices we use to build it.

    That flat structure comes with real product ownership. You won’t just be handed tickets — you’ll help define the “what” and the “why” alongside product owners, take features from intent through to production, and own the quality and outcome of what you ship. Responsibility here isn’t diffused across handoffs; it’s concentrated with the engineer who sees the work through.

    This is a great opportunity for someone who wants to give, learn, and grow alongside amazing, highly experienced people — and to put their mark on a fast-growing company on the path to becoming a global industry leader.

Where is this role located?

    This role is remote, with the option to work from one of our Sofia-based offices whenever you like. We offer flexible work hours, and our interview process is entirely remote.

Benefits and perks of working at AMPECO

    • The opportunity to join a fast-growing company on the path to becoming a global industry leader, working with amazing, highly experienced people.
    • Remote work with the option to work from one of our Sofia-based offices, plus flexible work hours.
    • A bonus day off to celebrate your birthday, and 5 additional vacation days per year after your first year with the company.
    • Social events and awesome team buildings.
    • Medical insurance for you and your family, with great coverage.
    • Monthly shared mobility allowance (covers Spark and GOeGO).
    • EV week — you get a company electric car for yourself for a week every 1–2 months.
Our team at AMPECO is deeply committed to our mission and we're looking for like-minded individuals eager to give, learn and grow with us. If you're passionate about innovative technology and want to make a real impact in the e-mobility sector, we want to hear from you. Join AMPECO in building the future of EV charging!
Our interview process is entirely remote. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.

With 70 chapters and a presence on 350 college campuses across North America, the AMA fosters a vibrant community of marketers. The association's philanthropic arm, the AMA’s Foundation, is inspiring a more diverse industry and ensuring marketing research impacts public good.

AMA views marketing as the activity, set of institutions, and processes for creating, communicating, delivering, and exchanging offerings that have value for customers, clients, partners, and society at large.   • Chapter Growth + Process Improvement
    • Identifies and implements improvements to chapter programs, policies, and operational processes to enhance the volunteer experience and organizational effectiveness.
    • Partners with the Senior Director, Membership and cross-functional teams to identify and implement opportunities that strengthen member engagement, support membership growth and retention, and leverage Professional Chapters as a key touchpoint in the AMA member experience, evolving the role to meet the changing needs of the association and its members.
    • Responds to chapter inquiries and provides guidance on chapter operations, development, growth, and revitalization in collaboration with the PCC.

About the Team

The Partners Team plays a critical role in extending that impact. We build and scale mutually beneficial relationships with leading LMSs, LXPs, HR platforms, and technology partners that distribute, bundle, or refer to OpenSesame's enterprise learning solutions globally. Our mandate is to create a scalable, tiered partner ecosystem that fuels indirect revenue, amplifies partner-led go-to-market motions, and delivers a world-class partner experience.

As Director of Strategic Partnerships, you will act as the architect and leader of this ecosystem, connecting strategy to execution, partners to product, and opportunity to revenue. You are a hands-on, player/coach leader who builds systems, drives outcomes, and leads by example.

You will define and evolve OpenSesame’s partner strategy, lead a global team of Strategic Partner Managers, own the programmatic maturity of the partner ecosystem, and serve as an executive-level partner to both internal leaders and external stakeholders.

Performance Objectives

Establish Strategic Clarity & Ecosystem Understanding (0–60 Days)

  • Build deep working knowledge of OpenSesame’s partner ecosystem by meeting with the top 30 partners to understand their business models, goals, performance metrics, and integration requirements.
  • Review existing partner processes, systems, reporting, and playbooks to identify scalability gaps and execution friction.
  • Develop strong relationships with Strategic Partner Managers by observing partner touchpoints, including QBRs, enablement sessions, and joint planning meetings.
  • Gain fluency in OpenSesame’s value proposition, competitive positioning, and integration approaches — including tradeoffs across different partner requirements.

Drive Program Insight & Early Impact (60–90 Days)

  • Conduct and present a comprehensive SWOT analysis of the partner program, identifying growth blockers, operational inefficiencies, risks, and expansion opportunities.
  • Define the critical path for ecosystem growth aligned to OpenSesame’s 30%+ annual revenue targets.
  • Begin contributing individually to high-impact partner engagements, including QBRs and strategic planning sessions.
  • Review and evaluate partner tiering, incentives, joint value propositions, and performance metrics to assess alignment with long-term strategy.
  • Lead executive-level partner meetings, onsite visits, and strategic presentations.
  • Establish clear expectations, goals, and communication cadences with your global team.
  • Demonstrate early improvements in partner contribution metrics, including sourced revenue, influenced revenue, partner satisfaction, and depth of collaboration.
  • Act as a trusted contributor to the Senior Management Team, helping refine OKRs, inform strategy, and represent the partner ecosystem across the business.

Scale the Partner Operating System (90–180 Days)

  • Deliver a comprehensive three-year partner ecosystem strategy, outlining revenue milestones, GTM alignment, resourcing needs, operational improvements, and partner experience enhancements.
  • Present cross-functional recommendations to Sales, Marketing, Product, and Operations to unlock partner-led growth.
  • Launch key initiatives to evolve the partner program, such as improved onboarding workflows, refined partner tiers, enhanced enablement, and optimized operating processes.
  • Establish a scalable partner governance model covering roadmap visibility, escalation paths, joint planning, and communication cadences.
  • Build and launch internal and external partner reporting systems that track performance, pipeline, onboarding, enablement, and strategic outcomes.
  • Optimize and operationalize the Partner Playbook to document best practices for forecasting, escalations, enablement, and partner management.
  • Demonstrate measurable improvements in indirect pipeline contribution, funnel conversion, and partner engagement.
  • Collaborate with Partner Operations to define scoring rubrics and threshold criteria for future partner tiers.

Deliver Sustained Ecosystem Growth (12+ Months)

  • Serve as the executive owner for OpenSesame’s most strategic partners, leading roadmap alignment, joint business planning, and high-impact GTM initiatives.
  • Drive ecosystem-led revenue growth through mature partnership models, strong executive relationships, and repeatable partner motions.
  • Demonstrate sustained improvements in partner satisfaction, revenue contribution, and long-term collaboration depth.
  • Lead complex partnership opportunities end-to-end, including structuring partnership models, executive negotiations, onsite engagements, and strategic presentations.
  • Continue evolving the partner ecosystem to support OpenSesame’s global scale, product strategy, and long-term growth.

What Success Looks Like

  • Partners consistently generate meaningful sourced and influenced revenue.
  • The partner ecosystem operates with clarity, repeatability, and strong executive trust.
  • Strategic partners see OpenSesame as a core, long-term growth partner.
  • Internal teams experience strong alignment and confidence in partner-led GTM motions.
  • The partner program scales with structure, accountability, and measurable impact.

You might notice we don’t list a traditional set of requirements or buzzwords here. That’s intentional. We’re looking for proven examples from your career that show you can build systems, lead teams, scale ecosystems, and drive results.

When you look back a year from now, you’ll know you’ve made OpenSesame stronger, faster, and more scalable because of the partner organization you built and led.

About the Role

The Senior Healthcare Supply Chain Analyst III (Information Technology/Clinical Information Systems) works with other Staritas team members on large projects related to healthcare information technology, systems, and software. Examples include pharmacy automation solutions, clinical decision support systems, laboratory information systems, enterprise imaging software solutions, artificial intelligence technologies, and other software-based solutions commonly used in healthcare environments. The Senior Analyst III works closely with healthcare facility clinicians, clinical engineers, IT teams, and other stakeholders to identify, evaluate, and compare healthcare IT technology vendors and solutions. The Senior Analyst III plays a leading role in researching new and emerging IT technologies, tracking industry trends, and facilitating client engagement with Staritas product offerings. Using knowledge gained from research, experience, and client feedback, the Senior Analyst III also recommends topics for new Staritas reports and initiatives to assist Staritas members. As a member of the Staritas Global Supply Chain Solutions team, the Senior Analyst III plays a major role in charting the direction of the team with a focus on the evolving Information Technology needs of Staritas member organizations.

Essential Functions

  • Identifies purchase, lease/rental, and service contract pricing benchmarks related IT systems and services, using Staritas' internal database applications.
  • Analyzes information technology price quotations for equipment and software from a financial perspective and provides hospitals with information and resources to facilitate price negotiations with vendors.
  • Researches new and emerging IT hardware, software, and services, and provides information on technical specifications, pricing, and safety.

For People is a team of humans. We place a significant amount of emphasis on positive work-life balance, setting healthy expectations, and making sure our loved ones are taken care of first. That means picking a child up from school during the day or going for a mid-day walk is okay!

Position Summary

We are looking for a Senior Talent Acquisition Specialist to join our growing team.

In this role, you will manage full-cycle recruiting for multiple concurrent searches, partnering with hiring managers to build pipelines and optimize our growth-stage hiring systems. You will balance hands-on sourcing with a strategic focus on data, process, and candidate experience. Beyond execution, you will own the end-to-end candidate and manager journey, directly shaping our employer brand and leaving your fingerprints on the recruitment process itself.

The ideal candidate is a proactive, detail-oriented recruiter who thrives on building relationships, enjoys solving sourcing puzzles for hard-to-fill roles, and knows how to keep multiple searches moving without sacrificing quality or candidate experience.

Note: Practice Better is a remote-first company with team members across North America. However, this particular role is currently open to Canadian-based candidates only, and preference will be given to applicants legally authorized to work in Canada.

What You'll Be Doing

  • Own and lead full-cycle hiring across multiple concurrent searches, from intake through offer and close, balancing hands-on execution with pipeline strategy and stakeholder alignment
  • Partner closely with hiring managers to shape role scope, define success profiles, and calibrate expectations, ensuring we are targeting the right talent from the outset
  • Build and execute sourcing strategies to attract top talent, especially for hard-to-fill roles, using a mix of outbound approaches, networks, referrals, and creative tactics
  • Manage and continuously improve our use of our ATS (Greenhouse), keeping pipelines, stages, and reporting clean and up to date
  • Establish and refine interview frameworks, scorecards, and calibration practices to ensure high-quality, equitable, and consistent hiring outcomes
  • Champion an exceptional and inclusive candidate experience, acting as a steward of our values and ensuring thoughtful, bias-aware hiring practices
  • Contribute to and help shape our employer brand by staying close to market trends and ensuring our narrative resonates with top talent
  • Track, analyze, and communicate recruiting metrics, using data to identify bottlenecks, improve conversion, and drive accountability across the hiring process

What You Bring

  • 5+ years of full-cycle recruiting experience in a startup or high-growth SaaS environment
  • Proven ability to manage a high volume of concurrent searches across multiple functions without sacrificing candidate experience or hiring quality
  • Strong outbound sourcing skills, with the ability to build creative pipelines for hard-to-fill or niche roles rather than relying solely on inbound applicants
  • Experience building or improving recruiting processes, such as structured interview scorecards, hiring manager training, or calibration sessions
  • A track record of DEI-focused or bias-aware sourcing & hiring practices
  • Strong communication and stakeholder management skills, with a bias for clarity and action, including with senior leaders
  • Comfort with data: pulling, interpreting, and acting on recruiting metrics like time-to-fill, source of hire, and pipeline conversion
  • Proficiency with an applicant tracking system (Greenhouse or Pinpoint experience preferred)
  • Analytical, curious, and adaptable; you seek solutions, not perfection

Bonus Points

At Practice Better, we believe in pay transparency, equity, and fairness. We benchmark compensation against similar-stage, high-growth SaaS companies in both Canada and the United States and review our salary bands regularly to ensure they remain competitive and aligned with market trends.

Each role has a defined pay range based on its level, scope, and geographic location. Final offers are determined by several factors, including experience, demonstrated skills, and location, to ensure consistency and equity across our team.

Final offers may vary depending on factors such as location, skills, depth of experience, and relevant certifications. All compensation ranges are reviewed regularly and may evolve over time to reflect changes in the market.

We offer a robust benefits package for full-time, permanent employees, including health, dental, and vision coverage from day 1, as well as RRSP matching, generous paid parental leave, and annual learning stipends.

Remote-First, Connected Culture

Our remote-first model gives you autonomy and flexibility, with optional access to our downtown Toronto office for in-person collaboration. We also host regular off-sites and team gatherings across North America, because connection, creativity, and shared moments matter.

Wellness and Growth

  • Unlimited vacation, built on trust, clear expectations, and real support for taking time off

Thriving at Practice Better

At Practice Better, you are not just an employee. You are part of a mission-driven community dedicated to helping others thrive. You will be trusted with autonomy, encouraged to take ownership, and supported by a team that values curiosity, compassion, and meaningful results.

We believe great culture and great performance go hand in hand. Delivering on our commitments is how we earn the trust of our practitioners and continue to expand our impact. Here, you will find the freedom to experiment, a focus on follow-through, and the opportunity to grow, along with the satisfaction of knowing your work directly improves lives every day.

Our Commitment to Diversity, Equity & Belonging

We know innovation happens when diverse perspectives come together. Practice Better is committed to fostering an inclusive environment where every team member feels valued, supported, and empowered to contribute their best.

If you do not meet every requirement listed above, we still encourage you to apply. Research shows that underrepresented groups often hesitate unless they feel 100% qualified. We are far more interested in your potential, curiosity, and alignment with our values.

We are committed to building a workplace where everyone can do the best work of their careers. We welcome applicants of all backgrounds, experiences, and abilities. Accommodations are available throughout the interview process upon request.

jobs.description:
Please submit your CV in English and indicate your level of English proficiency.

Mindrift connects specialists with project-based AI opportunities for leading tech companies, focused on testing, evaluating, and improving AI systems. Participation is project-based, not permanent employment.

What this opportunity involves

We're building competitive-programming problems and their automatic graders (test cases + checkers) used to train advanced AI coding models. You'll create problems, write both correct and deliberately-wrong solutions, and design the tough test cases that catch subtly-broken code. Your work is what makes the training signal trustworthy.

To apply, share: your competitive-programming handle(s) + current/peak rating, any problem-setting experience, and IOI/ICPC/olympiad history.

What you'll do

  • Write original algorithmic problems — clear statement, sound constraints, an intended solution;
  • Write correct solutions in C++ and Python;
  • Write realistic wrong solutions (common mistakes) to test against;
  • Build and harden test cases: generators, edge cases, stress and "hacking" tests;
  • Write checkers/interactors (testlib) for problems with more than one valid answer;
  • Confirm the quality bar: correct solutions pass, wrong ones fail, within time limits.

What we look for

  • Strong competitive programming background, shown by a public profile — a Codeforces rating (see levels below), OR an IOI / ICPC / national-olympiad record;
  • Fluent contest C++ (STL, complexity); comfortable writing Python;
  • Can explain why a solution is wrong and build an input that breaks it;
  • Strong written English (C1+).

Levels (by Codeforces rating, or equivalent olympiad achievement):

  • Associate — 1700–2100 (Expert / Candidate Master): easier problems;
  • Expert — 2200–2600 (Master / Grandmaster): harder problems
  • Senior / Reviewer — 2600+ (Int'l Grandmaster) or IOI/ICPC medalist: hardest problems + quality review.

Nice to have

  • IOI / ICPC alumni and top competitive programmers especially encouraged to apply;
  • Experience setting or testing problems for real contests (Codeforces rounds, ICPC, national olympiads, online judges);
  • Testlib experience (checkers, validators, generators);
  • Experience creating data for LLM code benchmarks or similar RL / evaluation datasets.

How it works

Apply → Pass qualification(s) → Join a project → Complete tasks → Get paid

Project time expectations

For this project, tasks are estimated to require around 10-20 hours per week during active phases, based on project requirements. This is an estimate, not a guaranteed workload, and applies only while the project is active. Tasks must be submitted by the deadline and meet the listed acceptance criteria to be accepted.

Compensation

Paid per accepted task. Your rate depends on the qualification tier you reach and how efficiently you complete tasks — up to the equivalent of $90/hr. Because payment is per task, a faster pace raises your effective hourly rate.

jobs.description:
Columbia University School of Professional Studies (SPS) seeks candidates for the role of Adjunct Lecturer to develop and teach Raising Capital, a graduate-level course in the M.S. in Technology Managementprogram.

The course development process is online (remote) and requires 2 semesters, beginning at the start of the Fall 2026 semester and concluding at the end of the Spring 2027 semester. The course will first potentially be taught in either the Summer 2027 semester or the Fall 2027 semester. The course will be developed for both Online (remote) and On-Campus instruction.

Raising Capital provides a fundamental understanding of the capital raising process for early-stage founders and technology leaders who are seeking seed and growth capital for their innovative solutions. The course will begin with a survey of the state of the current fund-raising market and the types of capital available in the market along with their relevant terms. The course will then dive deeper into the various aspects of the fund-raising process including 1) fund-raising strategy development, 2) engagement tactics with the fund-raising community, and 3) understanding term sheets and financing agreements. Students will also develop their pitch materials as they progress through the course and be expected to present or submit their pitch materials along the way.

Course Development Responsibilities

  • Develop course objectives that align with program-wide learning outcomes
  • Create activity maps tying course activities to objectives, ensuring industry relevance
  • Draft a detailed syllabus (course description, schedule, grading rubric, and assessments) for review and approval by the Program Curriculum Committee and the Committee on Instruction (COI)
  • Collaborate with Instructional Design to develop course materials through a consultative process. This includes partnering on course development (aligning objectives, materials, and assessments), creating dynamic instructional media (videos, infographics, and interactive resources), maintaining established courses with updates and troubleshooting, and receiving just-in-time assistance for targeted needs

Instruction Responsibilities

  • Lead class lectures, instructional activities, and classroom discussions
  • Evaluate student work and assignments
  • Monitor student concerns and inquiries and serve as the first point of contact for student questions
  • Hold weekly office hours
  • Prepare, maintain, and enhance the course in Canvas, Columbia University’s learning management system
  • Adjunct Lecturers who are new to SPS must complete Canvas training
  • Attend program faculty meetings

Serving as an Adjunct Lecturer provides an outstanding opportunity to educate and mentor students as well as to form a rewarding professional relationship with Columbia University’s world-class faculty.

Columbia University SPS operates under a scholar-practitioner faculty model, which enables students to learn from faculty who have outstanding academic training as well as a record of accomplishment as practitioners in an applied industry setting.

Requirements

  • Graduate degree in IT (e.g., computer science, software engineering, AI), business management, finance, or other related disciplines
  • At least 15 years of industry experience with a focus on driving digital transformation and innovation processes in large corporations
  • Strong academic foundation in a relevant discipline
  • Demonstrated proficiency in subject matter relevant to the course
  • Professional experience and demonstrated success in an applied industry setting

Preferred Skills & Experience

  • 10+ years of relevant professional experience
  • 2+ years of teaching experience, ideally at the graduate level

Compensation Range

  • $5,000 - $6,000 for Course Development (split across 2 semesters)
  • $13,000 - $16,000 for Instruction

Note: Columbia University’s Policy on Remote Work states that anyone teaching online classes must reside in one of the following states: Arizona, California, Colorado, Connecticut, Delaware, the District of Columbia, Florida, Georgia, Hawaii, Illinois, Maryland, Massachusetts, Montana, New Jersey, New York, North Carolina, Oklahoma, Texas, Vermont, Virginia and Washington.

Review of applications begins immediately and will continue until positions are filled. All applicants must provide:

  • A CV inclusive of university teaching experience
  • A cover letter describing your interest in this course and relevant teaching experience

Columbia University is an Equal Opportunity Employer / Disability / Veteran

Columbia University has been a leader in higher education in the nation and around the world for more than 250 years. Through twenty professional master's degrees, courses for advancement and graduate school preparation, certificate programs, summer courses, high school programs, and a program for learning English as a second language, the School of Professional Studies transforms knowledge and understanding in service of the greater good.

About Mainspring

Mainspring Energy manufactures and delivers fuel-flexible, low-emissions local power solutions that rapidly add new capacity and deliver reliable, affordable, and sustainable electric power. The company began commercial shipments of its Mainspring Linear Generators in 2020 and today has hundreds of megawatts in advanced development and field operations for leading Fortune 500 companies, data centers, and utilities. Mainspring also partners with global energy leaders including AEP, NextEra Energy Resources, Schneider Electric, and more.

The core values that ground our work, guide our decisions, and connect us together:

  • Pragmatic Optimism
  • Excellence without Ego
  • Proactive Collaboration

Position Overview

Mainspring needs a role focused on building the Company’s utility and interconnection strategy capability for larger, more complex projects and customers.

This position of Interconnection Strategy Lead is intended to bridge project execution, utility strategy, transmission-scale readiness, internal workflow design, and requirements intelligence to support Mainspring scaling beyond one-off projects and manual coordination.

The role will support larger customer segments such as data centers, utilities, and enterprise accounts, while helping the organization prepare for utility-scale, transmission-adjacent, and geographically diverse deployments. It also includes strategic review and planning for interconnection across North America.

The purpose of this role is to translate utility, market, interconnection, and regulatory complexity into repeatable business processes, customer-ready guidance, and scalable internal systems.

This position focuses on developing a more programmatic capability that supports larger sites, more sophisticated customers, and increasing process complexity.

Responsibilities

  • Utility and Interconnection Strategy
  • Lead utility and interconnection strategy for complex customer opportunities, including large-load, utility-scale, and enterprise projects.
  • Evaluate site-specific interconnection pathways, utility requirements, and market-participation implications, including differences between market participant and non-market participant pathways where relevant.
  • Identify material cost, schedule, and technical risks early, including study triggers, protection requirements, relay requirements, and other constraints that can affect project viability.
  • Develop or coordinate alternative operating, engineering, and interconnection approaches where standard utility requirements create unacceptable delay or cost exposure.
  • Large-Site and Transmission Readiness
  • Support Mainspring’s transition from smaller distributed projects toward larger 10 MW-plus opportunities and other projects that may cross ISO, transmission, or additional utility thresholds.
  • Help define the technical and process capabilities required to succeed in larger projects, including OEM model availability, transmission-grid interaction understanding, and cross-functional readiness.
  • Coordinate with internal and external technical stakeholders to address issues related to power systems behavior, controls, grid interaction, and compliance expectations.
  • Contribute to readiness planning for markets and customers that require stronger utility-strategy sophistication, including enterprise accounts and island or nonstandard regions.
  • Regulatory and Compliance Readiness
  • Support internal understanding of utility, transmission, and relevant NERC considerations that may affect large-scale projects and customer diligence.
  • Help surface what information customers and internal teams will increasingly expect as project size and complexity grow.
  • Coordinate with internal compliance, controls, security, and technical stakeholders where interconnection, cyber, controls, or compliance considerations overlap.
  • Process, Workflow, and Systems Design
  • Design and improve repeatable workflows for interconnection and utility-related work in Jira, including issue types, note templates, required fields, statuses, milestones, and handoffs.
  • Replace manual and spreadsheet-based tracking where practical with clearer, auditable workflow structures that support scale.
  • Build practical instructions and operating methods that allow adjacent team members to contribute to opportunity scrubs, site reviews, and process execution more consistently.
  • Work with internal systems and operations stakeholders to connect interconnection workflows to broader tooling such as Jira and Procore.
  • Knowledge Management and Requirements Intelligence
  • Create and maintain reusable guidance, templates, and internal reference material for recurring interconnection and utility questions.
  • Support the development of a structured repository for utility documents, web links, meeting notes, and requirements records using Google Workspace and related tools.
  • Help define how AI-assisted tools can be used to standardize internal reports, reference documents, and customer-facing outputs while preserving required human review and information-security guardrails.
  • Reduce organizational dependence on tribal knowledge by converting recurring analyses into maintained, reusable assets.
  • Cross-Functional Leadership
  • Serve as a strategic partner across Sales, Interconnection, PM, PE, Controls, and other teams involved in opportunity evaluation and project execution.
  • Translate technical and regulatory issues into language that supports decision-making by commercial, delivery, and leadership stakeholders.
  • Help define priorities, clarify ownership, and advance work even where processes are immature or feedback loops are incomplete.
  • Contribute to the design of a more scalable operating model for utility and interconnection support as the company grows.
  • Leverage your mechanical prowess and unique skills to construct cutting-edge components and assemblies for our generators, following procedures while also identifying opportunities for innovation.
  • Conducting thorough inspections of test units and meticulously documenting your findings to provide crucial insights for our engineering team.
  • Proactively identify and implement improvements that enhance both the safety and efficiency of our groundbreaking work.

Learn more on Life at Coupa blog and hear from our employees about their experiences working at Coupa.
The Impact of a Lead Data Management Specialist at Coupa:

Coupa is hiring a Technical Lead, AI Data Governance to own the data governance and gateway strategy that makes the company’s growing portfolio of AI tools and agents safe to ship. The role makes sure the data flowing into Coupa’s GenAI and agentic applications is governed, trusted, and fit for purpose, and that the API gateway in front of LLM traffic enforces the policies that protect the company.

This is a senior individual contributor role reporting to the Director, Data Governance. The role partners daily with Enterprise Data Management, AI Delivery & Execution, and InfoSec.

What You'll Do:

    Own the AI-Readiness Layer for Coupa’s Data

  • Resolve the data fitness questions AI builders raise day-to-day: which data sources fit which AI use case, what can safely go into a prompt, which dataset is the source of truth for a given attribute, and what meets the freshness or accuracy bar for retrieval. The AI-readiness framework and source-of-truth designations this role owns produce those answers.
  • Define what AI-readiness means for an enterprise data asset (completeness, freshness, accuracy, lineage, consent, licensing, source-of-truth designation), and publish that framework as Coupa’s standard.
  • Drive extension of the data catalog into an AI asset inventory. Rate each in-scope asset as AI-ready, AI-restricted, or AI-prohibited, with documented criteria, owners, and review cadence.
  • Partner with Enterprise Data Management to ensure foundational data quality refreshes (third-party account and contact enrichment, dedupe, taxonomy, address standardization) flow downstream into the vector stores, RAG indexes, and prompt-time lookups AI applications depend on.
  • Connect the metric library to AI consumers: every number an AI tool surfaces traces back to a governed metric definition, with documented and testable lineage.
  • Define AI-aware data quality monitoring requirements.

    • Set AI Data Governance Standards and Policy

  • Author and maintain Coupa’s AI data governance playbook: acceptable use, data classification for AI consumption, prompt logging, human-in-the-loop expectations, and model deprecation policies.
  • Build and run intake and review for new AI use cases. Evaluate data sensitivity, source quality, source-of-truth alignment, and gateway requirements before launch. Target turnaround: five business days.
  • Translate compliance and regulatory requirements (GDPR, SOC 2, EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF) into operational standards the data and AI teams can apply.

    • Partner with AI Delivery & Execution

  • Embed in the AI Delivery & Execution team’s planning rituals, sprint reviews, and architecture discussions on a regular cadence.
  • Co-own the AI/API gateway. Define the governance policies, target outcomes, and observability requirements; the AI Delivery engineering team builds the applications that integrate with it.
  • Define gateway-level controls for PII detection and redaction, prompt sanitization, content filtering, and prompt/response logging. Translate compliance and policy decisions into specifications engineering can build.
  • Define observability and reporting requirements for the gateway: usage by team and application, anomaly alerts, per-model cost tracking, and SLAs for downstream consumers.
  • Pair with AI engineers on data sourcing decisions: which governed asset to draw from, which CDE definitions to honor, how to handle records that fall outside AI-ready criteria, and when to require a human-in-the-loop checkpoint.
  • Triage AI quality incidents jointly. Trace stale, wrong, or duplicated outputs through the gateway, RAG pipeline, and source records, and route fixes to the team best positioned to resolve them.

What You Will Bring to Coupa:

  • 8+ years of related experience, with at least 5 years as a Data Product Manager, Technical Program Manager, or comparable role owning data products and driving cross-functional implementation.
  • Track record shipping AI/ML solutions end-to-end in an enterprise environment: scoping with stakeholders, partnering with data and engineering teams, working through ambiguity, and measuring impact post-launch.
  • Working knowledge of LLM application patterns: prompt engineering, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG), embeddings, and agent frameworks. Familiarity with the common failure modes (hallucination, prompt injection, data leakage, training-data contamination).
  • Solid grounding in data governance principles and frameworks (DAMA-DMBOK, DCAM, or comparable). Hands-on history with data quality standards, CDE frameworks, source-of-truth designations, or metadata/catalog programs.
  • Familiarity with API governance platforms (the policy enforcement layer that sits in front of API traffic and applies authentication, rate limits, content filtering, and audit logging). Comfortable owning gateway strategy as a product and partnering with engineering on implementation.
  • SQL fluency sufficient to profile data quality directly against warehouse tables (Snowflake or comparable).
  • Working familiarity with GDPR, CCPA, and emerging AI regulation (EU AI Act, NIST AI RMF) at the level needed to apply them; legal-grade depth isn’t required.
  • Strong written communication. The role authors policies, playbooks, and decision memos that cross functional lines.

Job Description:

The Provider Network Representative is the frontline liaison between the World Trade Center Health Program (WTCHP) and participating healthcare delivery organizations.

The role is responsible for provider onboarding, education, issue resolution, relationship management, provider engagement and satisfaction, and coordination of operational support activities. The Representative partners with Provider Data, Credentialing, Contracting, Claims, Finance, Clinical Operations, Communications, and IT to deliver consistent, high‑quality provider experience and ensure operational excellence.

Key Outcomes & Success Metrics

  • Provider satisfaction & FCR: Achieve targeted satisfaction scores and first‑contact resolution rates; reduce escalations and repeat issues.
  • Onboarding timeliness: Meet/exceed SLAs for onboarding and participation activation; shorten cycle times and eliminate avoidable delays.
  • Issue resolution performance: Decrease average issue aging and backlog across claims, credentialing, enrollment, provider data, contracts, and portal support.
  • Portal adoption & engagement: Increase portal registration, use of self‑service features, EFT enrollment, and training attendance.
  • Communication effectiveness: Improve responsiveness and clarity of provider communications, job aids, and training materials.
  • Quality & compliance: Maintain audit‑ready documentation; sustain SLA compliance and quality scores.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Relationship Management & Account Ownership

  • Serve as the primary point of contact for assigned providers; conduct regular touchpoints and executive‑level check‑ins/QBRs as needed.
  • Track provider sentiment and satisfaction; identify themes and drive action plans with the Provider Network Supervisor.
  • Document all interactions, decisions, and follow‑ups in CRM/case management tools with clear, accurate notes.

Onboarding & Orientation

  • Coordinate end‑to‑end onboarding: welcome materials, portal registration, EFT setup, credentialing handoffs, and directory validation.
  • Standardize checklists, timelines, and handoffs with Credentialing, Provider Data, and Contracting to ensure accurate participation activation.
  • Monitor onboarding milestones and proactively remove blockers; communicate status and next steps to providers.

Education, Training & Communications

  • Deliver provider training (webinars, welcome packets, job aids) on program policies, billing requirements, and operational procedures.
  • Tailor content to provider segments and roles; measure adoption and comprehension via attendance, feedback, and follow‑up assessments.
  • Maintain a current library of FAQs, guides, and reference materials aligned to process changes.

Issue Intake, Escalation & Resolution

  • Resolve escalated provider issues related to claims, credentialing, EFT, enrollment, and portal access; triage and route effectively.
  • Follow defined escalation pathways; communicate resolution status, root cause, and prevention actions to providers and internal teams.
  • Perform root‑cause analysis for recurring issues and propose corrective actions; track remediation to closure.

Portal, EFT & Self‑Service Enablement

  • Promote portal features and self‑service workflows; assist with registration, user management, navigation, and troubleshooting.
  • Increase EFT adoption and ensure accurate banking/EFT data in coordination with Provider Data and Claims; support verification and updates.

Cross‑Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with Provider Data, Credentialing, Contracting, Claims, Finance, Clinical Operations, Communications, and IT to resolve issues and improve processes.
  • Represent provider needs in workgroups; drive action items to completion and report measurable outcomes.

Reporting, Analytics & Continuous Improvement

  • Maintain dashboards/logs for satisfaction, first‑contact resolution, onboarding timeliness, case aging, portal adoption, and SLA compliance.
  • Analyze trends to prioritize outreach, training topics, and process enhancements; share insights in huddles and business reviews.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement initiatives (templates, scripts, automation) to reduce cycle time and error rates.

Compliance, Policy & Documentation Standards

  • Ensure adherence to organizational policies and applicable regulations; maintain audit‑ready documentation and records.
  • Safeguard provider information (privacy/security); support audits and corrective action plans.

Trillium Health Resources is a Tailored Plan and Managed Care Organization (MCO) serving 46 counties across North Carolina. JOB SUMMARY

The AVP, Associate Director of EFD – Operations & Financial Strategy is responsible for operational excellence, financial governance, core-system ownership, data integrity, and strategic growth enablement within the Equipment Finance Division’s (EFD). This role oversees all operational functions, ensures accurate financial and tax processes, manages business-unit reporting and budgets, and leads the strategic evaluation of new products, industries, and operational capabilities. This role requires advanced operational leadership, strong cross functional collaboration and partnership, and a very proactive approach to efficiency optimization, KPI-driven performance management, and critical thinking-based decision making. This position will require extensive communication with all business units within Equipment Finance Division (EFD) and other internal departments within Stearns Bank.

RESPONSIBILITIES

Leadership & Operational Strategy

  • Provide discipline, vision, and oversight for EFD finance and operations functions, ensuring processes are standardized, controlled, transparent and responsive.

  • Build, measure and sustain accountability, urgency, precision, Gold Standard service, financial discipline, and process integrity.
  • Identify operational risks, implement controls, and ensure audit readiness.
  • Work with other departments to ensure all processes function seamlessly, setting and enforcing clear ownership, accountability, and performance expectations for the EFD Finance and Operations teams and function.
  • Serve on the EFD Leadership Committee to oversee strategic direction, operational performance, systems strategy and risk management of EFD with the other committee members collectively.
  • Provide high-impact strategic leadership and ensure team culture reflects accountability, communication, ownership, and performance excellence.

Core System Ownership & Technology Strategy

  • Serve as the business owner of the core EFD systems, including configuration, workflows, permissions, and integrations.
  • Oversee how data enters, moves through, and exits the core platform.
  • Ensure accurate and reliable data feeds the general ledger, regulatory reporting, analytics, reporting and enterprise systems.
  • Identify & lead key projects, transformational initiatives and cross functional workstreams.
  • Strategic management of system upgrades, enhancements, and new module implementations, along with configuration of new initiatives of the bank and division.

Financial Governance, Controls, and Budget Oversight

  • Develop, manage, and monitor the budget for EFD, ensuring that it aligns strategic objectives and present to EFD Leadership Committee
  • Lead annual budget creation and ongoing financial management for each business unit.
  • Manage proper business unit assignments for all EFD Finance and Operations resources and expenses.

  • Provide actionable insights based on trends, variances, and operational constraints.

Team Leadership & Development

  • Mentor and develop high-performing professionals within finance, operations, and the core-system.
  • Promote culture of urgency, precision, professional communication, and financial ownership.
  • Provide effective leadership and development for the EFD finance and operations owners and leaders including performance management, staffing, talent development, and cross training.
  • Model focused partnership level collaboration with internal teams, vendors, and customers and reinforce those behaviors across the team.
  • Demonstrate a continual professional self-improvement mindset through continued training and education.
  • Lead and manage under conditions of ambiguity and uncertainty.

Communication

  • Lead strategic meetings with executives, team leaders, and business partners to resolve bottlenecks, align priorities, and improve service delivery.
  • Demonstrate a senior leadership level communication, influence, and negotiation skills.
  • Consistently demonstrates high quality documentation and reporting skills.
  • Communicates KPIs/KRIs, challenges, and solutions effectively to senior management.

  • Presents confidently to senior leaders and large internal groups.

Core Competencies

  • Highly organized, detailed-focused, financially disciplined, and decision and execution orientated.
  • Service mentality balanced with accountability and a risk management perspective.
  • Strong collaborator who aligns with lending, credit, operations, finance/liquidity, legal, compliance and all other internal and external teams as necessary.

As a Star Tribune Top Workplaces award recipient and an award recipient of the Minnesota Business Magazine 100 Best Places to Work in Minnesota, Stearns takes pride in their team and holds their employees in extremely high regard. jobs.description:
About Utorg

Founded in 2019, Utorg builds the infrastructure for stablecoin payments: on- and off-ramps, self-custodial wallets, and crypto cards. Over 2 million users across 130+ countries already buy, hold, and spend crypto through our app. On the B2B side, the same rails power 2,100+ platforms, with $2.4B+ moved to date.

Fully MiCA-authorized across the EEA. PCI DSS Level 2 certified. Backed by Dragonfly, TA Ventures, and Hypra.

Location: Remote

Tech stack: TypeScript, Node.js, NestJS, PostgreSQL, TypeORM, NATS JetStream, Redis, Jest, Docker, Kubernetes, Google Cloud Platform.

Blockchains: EVM-compatible, Bitcoin-family, Tron, Solana, TON.

What you’ll do:
  • Own backend architecture across two large-scale microservice platforms (30+ and 25+ services) — from system design and API contracts to data flow and inter-service communication.
  • Lead complex integrations — payment providers, card issuers, blockchain networks, third-party APIs — and take full responsibility for their reliability in production.
  • Drive performance and scalability — identify bottlenecks, design caching strategies, optimize database queries, and ensure the platform handles growing load.
  • Shape technical direction — make architectural decisions, evaluate trade-offs, and influence the team’s engineering standards. You’ll partially offload the Tech Lead so the team can scale.
  • Build and improve AI-powered processes — our team actively uses LLM-based systems to automate operational and development workflows. You’ll contribute to and extend this direction.
  • Contribute to back-office frontends (~20% of your time) — maintain and extend React-based admin dashboards used by internal teams.
  • Own features end-to-end — from planning and architectural design to implementation, testing, production monitoring, and iterative improvement.
  • Collaborate closely with Product, QA, and cross-functional teams — produce clear technical documentation, participate in code reviews, and share knowledge.
  • Take part in a shared on-call rotation — roughly one week a month.
Who you are:
  • Technically strong with an architectural mindset — you don’t just write code, you design systems. You think about data flows, failure modes, and long-term maintainability before writing the first line.
  • Opinionated and able to defend your decisions — you bring an expert perspective to technical discussions and can articulate trade-offs clearly to both engineers and stakeholders.
  • Proactive problem-solver — you find issues before they become incidents and propose solutions without waiting to be asked.
  • Product-driven — most of your time goes into shipping features and solving real user problems, not open-ended refactoring.
  • Self-motivated and responsible — you thrive in small teams, enjoy autonomy, and take full ownership of the development process.
What you will bring:
  • 5+ years of production experience in backend development with Type Script/Node.js as the primary stack.
  • 2+ years with NestJS in production — modules, providers, middleware, guards, interceptors, microservice architecture with custom transports.
  • Deep PostgreSQL expertise — schema design, indexing (partial, GIN/GiST), query optimization, migrations with zero-downtime, database-per-service pattern.
  • Hands-on microservices experience — not a monolith split into modules. You’ve dealt with inter-service communication (RPC + pub/sub), message brokers, idempotency, eventual consistency, saga/outbox patterns.
  • System design experience — decomposing services, designing API contracts, data flow architecture, capacity planning. You can whiteboard a system and explain why you made each decision.
  • Complex integration experience — you’ve built and maintained integrations with third-party APIs, payment systems, or similar external services in production. You know how to handle retries, circuit breakers, and graceful degradation.
  • Performance engineering— profiling, caching strategies, load analysis, bottleneck identification. You can optimize a slow query and a slow service alike.
  • Production blockchain experience (MUST-HAVE) — you’ve worked with on-chain transactions, multiple networks, and real user funds. You understand HD wallets (BIP32/BIP39), smart contracts, ABI, ERC-20/SPL tokens, and the differences between account-based and UTXO models. Experience with libraries like ethers.js, viem, and solana/web3.js.
  • AI-driven development (MUST-HAVE) — you actively use AI tools (Claude, Copilot, Cursor) in your daily workflow. Beyond personal productivity, you have experience optimizing business or organizational processes with AI/LLMs—building automations, internal tools, or workflows powered by language models.
  • Strong testing discipline — unit tests (Jest), integration tests with real databases, microservice testing.
  • Security-conscious — in fintech and crypto, every code path can touch real user funds. You build accordingly.
  • Skilled in technical research — evaluating trade-offs, testing hypotheses, and making data-driven architectural decisions.
  • English proficiency at Upper-Intermediate. Fluent in the Russian language.
Nice to have:
  • Experience with NATS JetStream as a transport layer (streams, consumers, delivery policies).

jobs.description:
Recruiter – Talent Acquisition & Full-Cycle Recruiting

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Client Business Hours, with flexibility for interviews and candidate coordination

About the Role

At Pavago, we’re hiring a Recruiter / Talent Acquisition Specialist to own full-cycle recruiting across sourcing, screening, interviewing, candidate management, and offer coordination.

This is a hands-on, execution-focused recruiting role. You’ll work across multiple industries and positions, partnering directly with hiring managers and clients to understand what they need, build strong candidate pipelines, and move qualified talent through the hiring process efficiently.

You’ll own the recruiting lifecycle from job intake and sourcing through interviews, client presentation, and offer acceptance.

This role is ideal for someone who loves sourcing, communicates confidently with candidates and clients, and can manage multiple fast-moving searches without sacrificing candidate quality or follow-through.

What You’ll Own

Full-Cycle Recruiting

  • Manage recruiting from initial job intake through offer acceptance.
  • Partner with hiring managers and clients to understand:
    • Role requirements
    • Must-have qualifications
    • Ideal candidate profiles
    • Compensation expectations
    • Hiring timelines
  • Create and optimize job descriptions to improve visibility and applicant quality.
  • Develop recruiting strategies based on each role and target candidate market.
  • Maintain momentum throughout every stage of the hiring process.

Candidate Sourcing & Pipeline Development

Build strong pipelines of active and passive candidates using:

  • LinkedIn Recruiter
  • Indeed
  • Glassdoor
  • Boolean search
  • Niche job boards
  • Direct outreach and other sourcing channels

You’ll:

  • Develop targeted Boolean searches.
  • Identify candidates who closely match client requirements.
  • Conduct outbound candidate outreach.
  • Build pipelines for multiple open positions simultaneously.
  • Maintain talent pools for recurring hiring needs.
  • Adjust sourcing strategies when applicant quality or volume is below target.

Candidate Screening & Interviewing

  • Conduct structured phone and video interviews.
  • Evaluate candidates based on:
    • Relevant experience
    • Technical or functional fit
    • Communication ability
    • Career progression
    • Motivation and career goals
    • Alignment with client requirements
  • Ask targeted questions to validate resume claims and experience.
  • Identify potential concerns before presenting candidates to clients.
  • Administer assessments or screening exercises when required.
  • Prepare clear candidate summaries and recommendations.
  • Maintain detailed and accurate interview notes.

Candidate Experience & Communication

  • Keep candidates informed throughout the hiring process.
  • Set clear expectations around timelines and next steps.
  • Coordinate interviews across multiple time zones.
  • Prepare candidates for client interviews.
  • Follow up promptly after interviews.
  • Manage candidate questions and concerns professionally.
  • Maintain a responsive and positive candidate experience from first contact through offer.

Client & Hiring Manager Coordination

  • Provide clients and hiring managers with regular pipeline updates.
  • Present qualified candidates with clear supporting context.
  • Gather feedback following interviews.
  • Facilitate interview debriefs and hiring discussions.
  • Communicate market feedback when requirements, compensation, or candidate availability create hiring challenges.
  • Adjust sourcing and screening strategies based on client feedback.
  • Act as a reliable recruiting partner rather than simply forwarding resumes.

Offer Management & Hiring Support

  • Coordinate offer preparation and presentation.
  • Support compensation discussions and negotiations.
  • Maintain candidate engagement during the decision process.
  • Address potential offer concerns proactively.
  • Coordinate hiring documentation and onboarding handoffs.
  • Maintain communication through offer acceptance and start-date confirmation.

ATS & Recruiting Operations

Maintain accurate candidate and recruiting data inside ATS platforms such as:

  • Greenhouse
  • Lever
  • JazzHR
  • iCIMS
  • Similar applicant tracking systems

You’ll ensure:

  • Candidate stages are accurate.
  • Interview notes are complete.
  • Follow-ups are documented.
  • Rejected candidates are dispositioned appropriately.
  • Hiring managers have clear pipeline visibility.
  • Recruiting activity is organized and measurable.

Recruiting Analytics & Reporting

Track and report metrics including:

  • Time-to-fill
  • Time-to-hire
  • Candidate pipeline health
  • Source effectiveness
  • Interview conversion rates
  • Candidate response rates
  • Offer acceptance rates
  • Hiring progress

Use recruiting data to identify bottlenecks and improve sourcing and hiring performance.

Required Experience & Skills

Core Requirements

  • 2+ years of professional recruiting, talent acquisition, or staffing experience.
  • Hands-on experience managing multiple open positions simultaneously.
  • Experience with full-cycle recruiting.
  • Strong sourcing experience using LinkedIn Recruiter.
  • Strong knowledge of Boolean search techniques.
  • Experience conducting structured candidate interviews.
  • Strong candidate assessment and qualification skills.
  • Experience managing recruiting pipelines within an ATS.
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication skills.
  • Strong organization, follow-through, and attention to detail.
  • Ability to manage competing priorities in a fast-moving remote environment.
  • Availability during U.S. client business hours.

ATS & Recruiting Technology

Hands-on experience with one or more platforms such as:

  • Greenhouse
  • Lever
  • JazzHR
  • iCIMS
  • Similar ATS platforms

Experience with sourcing and recruiting tools such as LinkedIn Recruiter and major job boards is strongly preferred.

Nice-to-Have Experience

  • Agency recruiting or staffing experience.
  • High-volume recruiting experience.
  • Experience recruiting internationally or remotely.
  • Experience hiring across multiple functions or industries, including:
    • SaaS
    • Technology
    • Finance & Accounting
    • Sales
    • Marketing
    • Property Management
    • Professional Services
  • Experience working directly with U.S.-based hiring managers or clients.
  • Familiarity with recruiting analytics and performance metrics.
  • Understanding of employment law and hiring compliance.
  • Experience managing offer negotiations.

What Makes You a Strong Fit

You:

  • Enjoy sourcing rather than relying entirely on inbound applicants.
  • Know how to identify strong candidates quickly.
  • Can distinguish a genuinely qualified candidate from someone whose resume simply contains the right keywords.
  • Communicate confidently with candidates and hiring managers.
  • Follow up consistently without needing reminders.
  • Keep ATS records and pipelines organized.
  • Can manage multiple searches without losing track of candidates.
  • Balance hiring speed with candidate quality.
  • Take ownership when a search is struggling and adjust your approach proactively.

What a Typical Day Looks Like

Your day may include:

  • Reviewing priorities across multiple open positions.
  • Sourcing candidates through LinkedIn Recruiter and job boards.
  • Building Boolean searches for difficult-to-fill roles.
  • Reviewing inbound applications.
  • Conducting recruiter phone screens and video interviews.
  • Preparing candidate summaries and recommendations.
  • Coordinating interviews between candidates and clients.
  • Following up with candidates and hiring managers.
  • Updating ATS stages, notes, and recruiting activity.
  • Reviewing sourcing and conversion metrics.
  • Adjusting recruiting strategies based on pipeline performance.
  • Supporting candidates through offers and onboarding handoffs.

In short: you build strong candidate pipelines, identify the right talent, and keep the recruiting process moving from initial search through successful hire.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Time-to-fill and time-to-hire.
  • Quality of candidates presented.
  • Interview pass-through and conversion rates.
  • Candidate response and engagement rates.
  • Hiring manager/client satisfaction.
  • Candidate experience and responsiveness.
  • Offer acceptance rates.
  • Sourcing effectiveness.
  • Pipeline health.
  • ATS accuracy and documentation quality.

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Full ownership across the recruiting lifecycle.
  • Opportunity to recruit across multiple industries and functions.
  • Direct exposure to U.S.-based clients and hiring managers.
  • Hands-on experience with modern sourcing and recruiting tools.
  • Fast-paced environment with measurable impact.
  • Fully remote opportunity.
  • Strong career progression into:
    • Senior Recruiter
    • Talent Acquisition Partner
    • Recruitment Consultant
    • Recruiting Lead
    • Recruitment Manager

Spark Hire Intro Video

As part of the application process, you’ll be asked to complete a short Spark Hire intro video.

We’d like to hear about:

  • Your recruiting and talent acquisition background.
  • The types of roles and industries you have recruited for.
  • How many open positions you typically manage simultaneously.
  • Your hands-on experience with LinkedIn Recruiter and Boolean sourcing.
  • An example of a difficult-to-fill role and how you successfully built the candidate pipeline.
  • How you evaluate whether someone is genuinely qualified before presenting them to a hiring manager.
  • The ATS platforms you have used.
  • Your experience working directly with hiring managers or clients.
  • How you manage candidate communication and follow-ups across multiple active searches.
  • An example of a recruiting process or sourcing strategy you improved.
  • Your experience with offer management or candidate negotiations.

Keep your responses clear, concise, and conversational. We’re particularly interested in your sourcing ability, communication skills, recruiting judgment, organization, and ability to take ownership of multiple searches.

Completion of the Spark Hire intro video is required for your application to be considered.

Interview Process

  • Initial Phone Screen
  • Spark Hire Intro Video
  • Video Interview with Pavago Recruiter
  • Practical Recruiting Task – Boolean Search & Candidate Sourcing Exercise
  • Client Interview
  • Offer & Background Verification

Apply Now

If you have strong full-cycle recruiting and candidate sourcing experience, know how to build high-quality pipelines, and thrive in a fast-moving environment where hiring results matter, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply today and complete the required Spark Hire intro video to move forward in the hiring process.
